layout: Three equal square cells, ordered light / medium / heavy; preserve full transparent cell canvases.
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: a transparent GAME DAMAGE OVERLAY ATLAS, exactly three equal square cells in one horizontal row (3:1 aspect ratio, ideally 3072x1024).
The three supplied images are layout templates: image 1 LIGHT, image 2 MEDIUM, image 3 HEAVY.
Repaint those three overlays in the new treatment specified below. Left cell = image 1, center cell = image 2, right cell = image 3.
Preserve EACH template's crack paths, branch count, forks and relative placement as closely as possible WITHIN ITS FULL SQUARE CELL. Do not crop away empty margins or zoom the light crack to fill its cell. In light, the small three-arm fork lies around the center. Medium extends it through top, left, right and bottom including the short inward-facing upper-right branch. Heavy spreads the dense original network throughout the square.
The styling must read as cracks going INTO a colored enamel game enemy, not raised wires, golden plumbing, metallic rods or an ornamental frame. Smooth polished illustrated arcade art with deliberate angular fractures; no grain or tiny noise. Slight edge variation is allowed; preserve the same three layouts.
Output ONLY the fissures and their very narrow adjacent chipped edges on genuine transparent alpha. All space between fractures must be completely transparent. Do not draw enemy tiles, surfaces between cracks, a background, ground plane, labels, separators, numbers or checkerboard. No floating fragments outside the paths. No border.
All three cells must share the same treatment, and damage must clearly grow from light to medium to heavy.
TREATMENT A: FINE RECESSED CRACKS. Make the fissures distinctly thinner and more restrained than the reference art, about half the visible width. Very dark cool charcoal crevices with irregular tapered endpoints. Add only an intermittent hairline cool gray highlight along one inner edge to convey shallow depth. Most edges are dark; no cream/gold bevel, no broad white stroke. Clean, subtle cracks that integrate with the face of the enemy; still clear at 32 pixels. Heavy has the same extensive network but remains fine and understated.
supersedes: Square overlays recorded in damage-original-layout-sources.json. Fireball overlays remain unchanged.
